audits.claim: Distinguish Ashina (dynastic/clan designation) from modern retellings naming a she-wolf 'Asena'; an ancient witness for that personal name must be produced (to-verify).
audits.source_locator: Zhoushu (周書) 50, Türks (突厥) monograph, fetched complete: pedigree line 姓阿史那氏; first origin tale (牝狼 … 狼匿其中，遂生十男 … 阿史那即一也); second 索國/伊質泥師都 variant ending 然終狼種也; banner line 侍衞之士，謂之附離 … 蓋本狼生，志不忘舊. The wolf receives no personal name anywhere in this fetched text (bounded to this witness; see limits).
audits.source_excerpt: 突厥者，蓋匈奴之別種，姓阿史那氏 … 有牝狼以肉飼之 … 狼匿其中，遂生十男 … 阿史那即一也
audits.excerpt_commentary: Commentary, not source text. The excerpt is verbatim from the fetched Zhoushu 50 text (pedigree line plus the first origin tale); … marks omitted transmitted wording. Rendering: 'The Türks … are surnamed A-shih-na'; 'there was a she-wolf which fed it meat'; 'the wolf hid therein, and in time bore ten sons'; 'A-shih-na is one of them.' Bounded observation: the she-wolf receives no name in the two inspected witnesses (Zhoushu 50 and Suishu 84) — not a claim of global absence (see limits). Excerpt length: 7 whitespace-delimited words.
audits.retrieval_method: Direct fetch (curl) of the full zh.wikisource.org text of 周書/卷50 and 隋書/卷84, saved and read locally under reports/supplement-opencode-1/scratch/round5-07/ (zhou-shu-juan50.html, suishu-juan84.html); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asena fetched in full as tertiary modern-usage documentation; Semantic Scholar API checked for an open PDF of Golden 2018 (openAccessPdf status CLOSED); SAGE DOI re-attempted this round, again HTTP 403. The host WebSearch tool was unavailable this session (provider 5-hour quota exhaustion), so discovery used direct scholarly/public URLs only.
audits.basis: Two ancient primary witnesses were retrieved as complete texts and both leave the she-wolf unnamed while naming the clan: Zhoushu 50 (surname 阿史那 in the pedigree line; the wolf 牝狼 unnamed in both origin variants, each still concluding wolf descent, 然終狼種也) and Suishu 84 (平涼雜胡也，姓阿史那氏; 其後狼生十男，其一姓阿史那氏，最賢，遂為君長，故牙門建狼頭纛，示不忘本也 — the wolf bears ten sons, one of whom is surnamed Ashina; the wolf itself is again unnamed). This is exactly the textual situation the entry's line 81 calibration addresses: the ancient witnesses supply a clan designation, not a personal name for the ancestress. The modern-usage side is documented at tertiary level: the retrieved Wikipedia article 'Asena' names the she-wolf, states the ancestress is 'mentioned, yet unnamed in two different Wolf Tales' (citing Golden 2018), and footnotes Ziya Gökalp's early-20th-century derivation 'Çinlilere göre (Asena=Kurt)', i.e. the name circulates in modern retellings, including nationalist-era ones, not in the Chinese witnesses consulted. Scope of support: the distinction and the evidentiary-burden instruction are supported for every witness actually consulted (Zhoushu 50, Suishu 84); this is not a demonstration that no ancient witness anywhere names the wolf, and the entry's (to-verify) flag stands for exactly that open question.
audits.coupling_implication: Myth/reception era coupling: 'Asena' can be used in modern-reception or fictional layers but must not be written into the early-medieval witness layer as an attested historical detail; clan designation and ancestress personal name are different layers of the same narrative and must not be merged when the descent myth is coupled to legitimation claims.
audits.limits: Absence from the retrieved texts cannot prove the name never existed in any ancient witness (only Zhoushu 50 and Suishu 84 retrieved; Beishi 99 wikisource page was fetched but is a stub containing no Türks monograph text, so a third ancient witness remains unchecked this round). Texts were read via modern wikisource base editions, not diplomatic editions or manuscript collation; a variant reading in another witness cannot be excluded. Golden 2018 remains closed (HTTP 403 re-attempted 2026-10-17; Semantic Scholar openAccessPdf CLOSED; no institutional access here), so the entry's cited comparator is still verified only through secondary echoes. Modern-usage documentation is tertiary (Wikipedia). Discovery was narrowed by the WebSearch provider outage; passages for the parent's independent re-fetch: zh.wikisource.org/wiki/周書/卷50 and zh.wikisource.org/wiki/隋書/卷84, plus en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asena.

audits.claim: Clauson (1972:594a, s.v. kut) traces a semantic range from heavenly favor through good fortune to happiness, with differing later developments including soul/life-force senses in some languages.
audits.source_locator: Clauson, An Etymological Dictionary of Pre-Thirteenth-Century Turkish (Oxford: Clarendon/OUP 1972), printed p.594, running head 'MON. ĠD': s.v. kut, entry opening in column 594a (above it the tail of 2 ka:t 'berry'), continuing into 594b and ending before the ka:d- preliminary note; confirmed by direct visual inspection of the repository scan's leaf image 0638.
audits.source_excerpt: kut originally in a rather mystical sense 'the favour of heaven', thence, less specifically 'good fortune' … thence, more generally, 'happiness' … in one or two languages, esp. in NE, it seems rather to mean 'soul, life force'.
audits.excerpt_commentary: Commentary, not source text. Verbatim as read on the leaf image 0638 of printed p.594 (column 594a; the OCR text agrees on wording). The first … omits 'and the like, and'; the second … omits 'In KB, where it is regarded as syn. w. Ar. dawla, it came to mean, more neutrally, fortune, either good or bad. S.i.a.m.l.g., usually for good fortune, happiness and the like, but'. Excerpt length: 38 whitespace-delimited words.
audits.retrieval_method: archive.org item metadata checked (access-restricted-item absent); the item's djvu.txt OCR (5.8 MB) downloaded to reports/supplement-opencode-1/scratch/round5-07/clauson-edpt.djvu.txt and the kut entry located by local grep; the scan's conflicting page metadata (page_numbers.json says image leaf 638 = printed 594, while OCR pageindex byte ranges place the entry text at stream position 684 and a stray '594 MON. GD' marker precedes it) was resolved by rendering leaf images via BookReaderImages.php and visually inspecting leaf 0638 (folio '594', kut entry opening column a) and leaf 0684 (folio 640, koṗ- entries), establishing that the OCR text stream is offset ~46 leaves from the image sequence and that page_numbers' image-based mapping is the correct one.
audits.basis: The entry text was retrieved twice over — as OCR and, decisively, as the page image of printed p.594 — and every element of the claim is verbatim on the page: 'originally in a rather mystical sense the favour of heaven' (heavenly favor), 'thence, less specifically good fortune and the like' (good fortune), 'thence, more generally, happiness' (happiness); 'in one or two languages, esp. in NE, it seems rather to mean soul, life force' (differing later developments in some languages). The same entry instantiates further differing developments the claim summarizes under that rubric: KB usage as neutral 'fortune', either good or bad; 'majesty' as attribute of divine personages (anıp uluğ kutıṇa; kaŋım kutı 'His Majesty my father'); a küt 'element' technical usage in astronomical texts; Old Turkic inscriptional citations qut at I E 31 ('Umay teg ögüm qağu:n kuṭıṇa: because my lady mother, who resembles (the goddess) Umay, enjoyed the favour of heaven'), I S 9, II N 7, II E 35, and IrkB 2 kut beṛgey men — independently corroborating the qut locators used by TURK-02/03/04. The prior row's only retrieved echo (Zarrinkoob & Toğay, dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/2915983, table row 'Clauson,1971, s. 594 — سعادت و خوشبختی') is consistent with the p.594 happiness gloss; its '1971' is a secondary-source misdate, the book itself being the 1972 printing.
audits.coupling_implication: Lexical-range vs political-gloss coupling: the entry's 'divine mandate' gloss is a context-dependent political rendering of a word whose dictionary range runs from heavenly favour through fortune to happiness (and, in some languages, soul/life-force), so the design coupling superhuman favor → provisioning/protection → legitimate rule rests on attested sense stages without requiring identification with Chinese tianming; era stratification inside one entry (Old Turkic inscriptional favour vs KB and later Osm./Çağ. developments) supports the entry's warning against projecting one sense onto all periods.
audits.limits: The text was read from a third-party repository scan (libgen.lc-sourced archive.org copy) of the 1972 OUP printing, verified against the leaf image rather than a library-held original; isolated OCR garbles (e.g. 'mafesty' for 'majesty', 'vvither' for 'wither') were resolved by image inspection, and the scan's own page-index/leaf-order metadata is internally inconsistent (OCR text stream offset ~46 leaves from image leaves) — the parent's independent re-fetch should use the leaf-image route (BookReaderImages.php, file stem 'Sir Gerard Clauson - An Etymological Dictionary of Pre-thirteenth Century Turkish (1972, Oxford University Press) - libgen.lc', member _0638.jp2) or the details-page viewer at leaf 638. The '594a' column letter was confirmed visually (entry opens in the left column under the folio '594'); a fresh photographic copy of the OUP original was not available in this environment.
